sentences.text: Heard finally with consent of the learned counsel for the parties.

2. By this appeal, appellant has challenged the judgment and award dated 04.04.2019 passed by the reference Court in reference under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act 1894 (for short, 'the Act of 1894'), filed by the claimant/land owner.

The Acquiring Body has filed this appeal contending that the reference Court has wrongly determined the market price of the acquired land and has granted excessive and exorbitant compensation to the respondent nos.1 and 2.
0202FA179-22.odt 2 Judgment 3.
The land of respondent nos.1 and 2 from Gat no.215 admeasuring 49 Are situated at Mouza Sawargaon, Tahsil Kalamb, District Yavatmal was acquired for the Bembla Project, Yavatmal.
The notification under Section 4 of the Act of 1894 was published in the Government Gazette in the year 2007.
The reference Court has granted compensation at the rate of Rs.4,20,000/- per Hectare alongwith 30% solatium and 12% additional component.

Being aggrieved thereby, the acquiring Executive Engineer, Bembla Project, ... vs Gajanan Shyamrao Bhongade And Others on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52765562/

4. Shri Parijat Pande, learned counsel for the respondent nos.1 and 2 submits that an identical appeal being First Appeal No.1235 of 2018 [Vidarbha Irrigation Development Corporation,
Yavatmal & Another Versus Mangala Pramod Uttarwar & Others ] arising out of the judgment and award passed by the reference Court pertaining to same Section 4 notification was decided and dismissed by this Court on 07.05.2024 whereby the compensation granted by the reference Court was maintained.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is specifically pointed out that in respect of the acquired land forming the subject matter of First Appeal No. 624 of 2021 and covered by the same Section 4 notification, the acquiring body and the claimants have arrived at an amicable settlement before the Lok Adalat.

In terms of the said settlement, the acquiring body has unequivocally agreed to pay compensation at the rate of Rs.4,20,000/- per Hectare as the market value of the land situated at Mouza Sawargaon acquired under the aforesaid Section 4 notification.
0202FA179-22.odt 3 Judgment 5.

Smt. Ira Khisti, learned counsel for the appellant/acquiring body does not dispute the aforesaid position and submits that the instant appeal can be decided on the basis of judgment in First Appeal No.1235 of 2018 referred above.
6. I have gone through the record and proceedings.
A perusal of the record reveals that the land situated at Mouza Sawargaon is acquired for the same purpose.
It has come on record that the acquisition was for the construction of a canal.
It is, therefore, apparent on the face of the record that a small extent of the land was acquired in each case.

In respect of the land situated at same village, relying upon other judgments of the Reference Court, the market price of the dry-crop land has been determined @ Rs.4,20,000/- per hectare, and for seasonally irrigated land @
Rs.6,30,000/- per hectare.
The parties have adduced evidence.

On the basis of the evidence,
similarity between the lands has been established.
Similarly, the evidence has not been adduced by the appellants to rebut all these facts.
The compensation for similarly situated lands needs to be uniform.
The Court has to ensure that there shall be no discrimination between the two landowners while awarding the compensation.

In my view, therefore, this appeal is squarely covered by the decision rendered by this Court in First Appeal No.1235 of 2018 with connected matters by judgment dated 07.05.2024 which was decided by considering the judgment in First Appeal No.1737/2019 [Vidarbha Irrigation Development Corporation & Anr. Vs. Jayantilal Jethalal Rupali & Ors. with connected appeals, decided on 07.05.2024].
0202FA179-22.odt 4 Judgment 7.

entities.text: Vidarbha Irrigation Development Corporation & Anr. Vs. Jayantilal Jethalal Rupali & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of this, there is no reason to take a different view and I conclude that the market price of the dry-crop land determined by the Reference Court @ Rs.4,20,000/ per hectare, and for seasonally irrigated land @ Rs.6,30,000/- per hectare is just, proper and reasonable.
As such, I do not see any substance in this appeal.
The appeal is accordingly dismissed.
No order as to costs.
